quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What can goggles protect?

options.text: Your eyes and your face.
Your face but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your face.
Neither your face nor your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield can protect your entire face during a crash.

questions.question: How do you stop quickly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the front brake first.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When are motorcyclists safest?

options.text: When other motorists can see them.
When they ride faster than other vehicles.
When they ride on the side of the road.
When they ride on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When other motorists can see them.
questions.explanation: Safe riders make sure other drivers can see them. Use your headlight, brake light, and signals. Choose a good lane position to stay visible.

questions.question: What is true about most motorcycle crashes?

options.text: The riders had less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
They are caused by faulty ignition systems.
They happen because passengers distract the rider.
They happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: The riders had less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on that specific motorcycle. Be extra careful when riding a new motorcycle.

questions.question: How should you sit to control a motorcycle properly?

options.text: Sit so your arms can steer, not hold you up.
Sit far back on the seat so your arms stay straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms can steer, not hold you up.
questions.explanation: Sit so you use your arms to steer the motorcycle, not to support yourself. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: Which is NOT a characteristic of a responsible rider?

options.text: They can ride with awareness.
They can make good decisions.
They can follow through on their decisions.
They enjoy riding motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They enjoy riding motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Responsible riders ride with awareness, make good decisions, and follow through on those decisions. Whether they enjoy riding is not a characteristic of responsibility.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Distances are easier to judge than during the day.
A high beam headlight always makes it harder to see.
Use only one lane position.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use your high beam when there is no oncoming traffic. Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: Small vehicles like motorcycles can appear ______ and seem to travel ______ than they actually are.

options.text: farther away, more slowly
farther away, faster
closer, more slowly
closer, faster

questions.correctAnswerText: farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles can look farther away and seem to move more slowly than they actually do. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge a motorcycle's true location and speed.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do when riding behind a car?

options.text: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
Always ride on the far left of your lane.
Do not worry about your lane position.
Always ride on the far right of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, stay in the center of your lane. This position is most visible in the car's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Before riding, you should check all of the following except:

options.text: Fluids.
Headlight and taillight.
Turn signals.
Reflectors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, what should you see?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
Your arms.
The road in front of your motorcycle.
The side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust mirrors so you can see the lane behind you and beside you. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: Passing another vehicle.
When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's single brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers see it, especially when you slow down faster than they expect.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should not:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid sudden moves.
Use both brakes.
Brake quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake quickly.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently if you need to stop.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Which formation keeps riders in a group closest together?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered
questions.explanation: A staggered formation helps a group stay close together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding?

options.text: Your arms hold you up.
You can easily reach the controls.
Your arms are straight when holding the grips.
Your knees are away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can steer with your arms instead of using them to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Provide you with an escape route.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen, avoids surface hazards, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and check mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for traffic before moving into another lane.

questions.question: When riding in a group, why should inexperienced riders ride near the front?

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they are leading.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: Put less experienced riders just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can easily watch them.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen best?

options.text: Orange and red.
Green and blue.
Purple and gold.
Black and white.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green. These colors make you easier to see.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding—the wobble will likely stop by itself.
Brake quickly.
Slow down by closing the throttle.
Speed up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by closing the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up—this makes the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Lean forward and low. Pull off the road as soon as you can and check what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot avoid a slippery surface?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to your following distance during the day?

options.text: Use a longer following distance at night.
Use a shorter following distance at night.
Always use the same following distance day or night.
Following distance does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance in the dark because shadows and light are different. Use a longer following distance when riding at night than during the day.
